newsitem.title: BELGIUM: VIRGIN EXPRESS TRYING TO GET A MESSAGE ACROSS.
newsitem.headline: VIRGIN EXPRESS TRYING TO GET A MESSAGE ACROSS.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express said on Thursday it had boosted its advertising budget to make passengers in Europe realise that flying with no-frills airlines was cheaper.
"We have tripled the advertising budget since we took over," chief executive Jonathan Ornstein told Reuters in an interview.
Virgin Express was launched last April after Branson bought 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines (EBA).
"It's a big issue because quite frankly for me it is somewhat strange that with 80 percent lower fares I still have to go out and get people to get on the airplanes," he said.
He noted that people in Europe were not yet fully familiar with low-cost, low-fare airlines and often booked tickets with the traditional flag carriers.
He said Virgin Express had spent 24 million Belgian francs ($716,000) on advertising just in November.
He said the carrier was also planning television advertising and was looking at "non-traditional methods".
"We're going to set up an internet web page, I'd like to do ticket auctions on the internet," he said.
